title: SIP: Session Initiation Protocol
organization: dynamicsoft / Columbia University / Ericsson and others
subtitle: The signaling protocol behind Voice over IP (VoIP), video calls, and multimedia sessions across the Internet.
summary: SIP is a text-based protocol for setting up, changing and ending sessions between users, such as phone calls and video calls. It looks like HTTP: requests such as INVITE and BYE get numbered responses such as 180 Ringing and 200 OK. SIP only does the signaling; the audio and video itself travel separately, usually over RTP.

eli5.summary: SIP is how two devices agree to start a call: one rings the other, the other picks up, and later one says goodbye. The talking itself is sent by some other method.

tldr.problem: Two people on the Internet need a standard way to find each other and agree to start, change and end a call or other media session.
tldr.mechanism: User agents exchange text requests (INVITE, ACK, BYE, REGISTER and so on) and numbered responses, optionally through proxies and registrars, while the media flows separately.
tldr.outcome: SIP became the signaling standard for VoIP and video calling, with many later RFCs extending it.

facts.label: Methods in this RFC
facts.value: INVITE, ACK, BYE, CANCEL, REGISTER, OPTIONS

today: SIP is still the main signaling protocol for VoIP phone systems and for the links between telecom operators, and many later RFCs extend it. The RFC Editor lists over twenty RFCs that update RFC 3261, so it is rarely used alone. Browser calling in WebRTC generally leaves the choice of signaling open.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
SIP is a text-based signaling protocol for creating, modifying, and terminating multimedia sessions. It handles the setup and teardown of calls while the actual media (audio/video) flows via RTP.

SIP is the main signaling protocol for VoIP phone systems and is widely used between telecom providers. Its HTTP-like text format makes it easy to debug and extend.
sections.eli5: SIP is like the ringing and answering part of a phone call. It does not carry your voice. It only lets the two phones agree that a call is happening.

sections.title: SIP Methods
sections.content:
INVITEInitiate a session or modify existing one
ACKConfirm reception of a final response
BYETerminate a session
CANCELCancel a pending INVITE
REGISTERBind a SIP URI to a contact address
OPTIONSQuery server capabilities
sections.eli5: SIP has a few action words. INVITE means "want to talk?", BYE means "goodbye", and REGISTER means "here is where you can reach me".

sections.title: Architecture
sections.content:
SIP uses several network elements:

User Agent (UA)End device (phone, softphone) that initiates or receives calls
Proxy ServerRoutes requests on behalf of UAs, handles policies
RegistrarAccepts REGISTER requests and stores location bindings
Redirect ServerResponds with alternative contact addresses
B2BUABack-to-Back User Agent - sits in the call path (PBX, SBC)
sections.eli5: Some devices are the phones. Others are helpers in the middle: one passes your call along, one keeps a list of where everybody currently is, and one can say "try this other number instead".

sections.title: SIP Message Example
sections.content:
SIP INVITE Request (simplified)
INVITE sip:bob@example.com SIP/2.0
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP pc33.example.com;branch=z9hG4bK776
Max-Forwards: 70
To: Bob <sip:bob@example.com>
From: Alice <sip:alice@example.com>;tag=1928301774
Call-ID: a84b4c76e66710@pc33.example.com
CSeq: 314159 INVITE
Contact: <sip:alice@pc33.example.com>
Content-Type: application/sdp
Content-Length: 142

SIP's text format is deliberately similar to HTTP, making it accessible to web developers and easy to inspect with standard text tools.
sections.eli5: A SIP message is plain text that you can read, a bit like a letter with To, From and a call number at the top.

messages.label: INVITE (SDP offer)
messages.note: Starts the session and carries the caller's media description.

messages.label: 180 Ringing
messages.note: A provisional response: the phone is ringing.

messages.label: ACK
messages.note: Confirms the final response to the INVITE.

cells: Provisional: request received, continuing to process it
Success: the request was received, understood and accepted
Redirection: further action is needed to complete the request
Client error: the request has bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled at this server
Server error: the server failed to fulfil an apparently valid request
Global failure: the request cannot be fulfilled at any server
